title.narrative: Value-addition in Agriculture from small dams in Burkina Faso (ProValAB 2) - Activity ProValAB2/Value-addition in Agriculture from small dams in Burkina Faso
Värdeskapande nyttjande av små dammar i Burkina Faso (ProValAB 2)

description.narrative:
The overall goal of ProValAB2 was "The living conditions of households in the project intervention area have improved by exploiting water from small dams through the development of promising value chains.
The achievement of this overall goal was dependent on three (3) outcomes which are:
i) Users put in place good governance for the sustainable management of infrastructures, water resources and developed lands;
ii) Farmers increase quantitatively and qualitatively their agricultural, forestry/tree, pastoral and fish farming production;
iii) Producers and other players in value chains improve their economic and social performance.
9 expected Outputs;
(1) Agricultural and fish production capacities and means have improved,
(2) Water resources and developed agricultural land are better managed)
(3) Agricultural production and productivity have increased,
(4) The quantity of fish caught/produced/processed has increased,
(5) Producers ensure good post-harvest management of their products and increase the quantities sold,
(6) Stakeholders have better access to the market,
(7) Product supply has improved,
(8) Access to credit has improved,
(9) Women's economic status and social role have improved.
ProValAB2 intervened at 22 sites spread over 6 Regions (19 sites remained from ProValAB1, plus 3 new sites) out of which 7 were inaccessible by the time of programme closure due to severe security problems.
Information about the Contribution
The initial activity period of ProValAB2 was 2021-12-01 - 2024-12-31 and the agreement period was 2021-12-01 - 2025-06-30. The initial overall ProValAB2 programme implementation budget was 141 614 000 SEK, out of which 5% was to be funded by the Government of Burkina Faso and 95% by Sweden. (ProValAB2 was proceeded by a ProValAB 1 during 2018-2021, with a budget of some 67 MSEK).
Sweden decided in 2023 to phase out development cooperation with Burkina Faso in 2024. The contribution was then as per the Amendment 1 signed in May 2024 reduced from a total of 135 000 000 SEK to 114 261 601 SEK, out of which 109 500 000 SEK remained in the Government implementation component 1 (see below), down from 121 000 000 SEK. A special phaseout workplan and budget for 2024/2025 was developed. ProValAB2 was given priority among the remaining contributions in the Sida portfolio in Burkina Faso during 2024 (due to the negative consequences of interrupting ongoing construction & supply contracts, and the tangible livelihood benefits to the target group), and was allocated a 24 500 000 SEK disbursement during 2024 despite the 60% budget cutdown to the portfolio. The activity period remained unchanged, ending by 31st of December 2024 while the revised agreement period was shortened somewhat. Some funds were allowed to be used for the administrative closing activities in January - May 2025.
The contribution included the following components:
- Funds disbursed to Government of Burkina Faso to support activities (109 500 000 SEK disbursed)
- Funds handled by Embassy/ Sida for International Technical Assistance (Including part of National consultants) provided by NIRAS Consulting (4 271 171 SEK disbursed)
- Funds handled by Embassy for Studies, Monitoring, Evaluation & Audits. (371 299 SEK disbursed)
- Funds handled by Sida for audits in 2025 (289 648 SEK disbursed)
Sida disbursed the entire amended agreed amount. There was no interest or balance of Sida funds to be reimbursed, as confirmed by audits.
Information about partner
The agreement was signed with the Government of Burkina Faso represented by the Minister of Economy, Finances and Development. The Government has mandated the Ministry in charge of Agriculture through the General Directorate for the Promotion of Rural Economy to be responsible towards the Government for the implementation of the Project which is managed daily by the ProValAB management unit.
Phase out impact
The phaseout work plan and budget for 2024/2025 meant;
The objectives would not change, but the expected results per objective would not be achieved in terms of impact and quantity due to the suppression of certain activities (only contracts concluded and signed by the end of 2023 would be implemented):
-Cancellation of contracts relating to the Yaongo dam development works, approximately SEK 2 251 405 -Cancellation of all contracts signed in 2024 as part of the communication plan, SEK 553 215 -Nonrenewal of certain staff contracts SEK 170 56 -Reduction of the budget for international technical advisors by approximately SEK 3 754 656
The phase-out workplan of 2024/2025 set out to mitigate the following risks (and seemed to have succeeded to satisfaction, see further down):
- Nonachievement or weak achievements of results (including noncompletion of infrastructure) - Reputational damage for Sweden/Sida/the Embassy, the lead implementing partner, and its partners - Administrative risk for partners linked to human resources, contractual compliance linked to Sidas requirements for reporting, auditing, and possible repayment of unused funds - Corruption and misuse of funds - Failure by lead partner to honour commitments to local partners

Projektet Värdeskapande nyttjande av små dammar i Burkina Faso (ProValAB 2) syftar till att inom jordbruket få till ett mer effektivt utnyttjande av redan existerande vatteninfrastuktur i Burkina Faso. Det övergripande målet för projektet är: "Hushållen utvecklar livsmedelstryggheten på ett hållbart sätt och ökar sina inkomster genom att utnyttja vatten från små dammar, som ett resultat av stärkta värdekedjor".
Projektets förväntade utfall är: "Levnadsvillkoren för hushållen i projektets insatsområde har förbättrats genom att utnyttja vatten från små dammar som ett resultat av stärkta värdekedjor ". Projektet syftar till att vara genustransformativt och kommer att sträva efter att bidra till ekonomisk egenmakt för kvinnor och ungdomar som aktörer i dessa värdekedjor.
ProValAB2 kommer att implementeras i 19 områden fördelade på 6 regioner: Center, Center-East, Center-North, Center-West, East and Central Plateau. ProValAB2 är en del av en ansats för att utveckla vattentäkters potential och främja jordbruksekonomin genom att skapa mervärde inom jordbruksproduktionen. Den betonar integrerad resursförvaltning genom att främja rättvis tillgång och hållbar användning av vattenresurser för de olika användarna (jordbrukare med bevattnade grödor, uppfödare, fiskare, fiskodlare, förädlare av jordbruks- och fiskeriprodukter, samt vattenanvändare/hushåll som använder dammar). Projektet är förenligt med prioriteringar inom jordbrukssektorn, som fokuserar på vattenförvaltning, mekaniserad teknikutveckling, utökad produktion och påskyndad bearbetningshastighet för jordbruksprodukter. Projektet bidrar till genomförandet av målen för hållbar utveckling, särskilt mål 1, 2, 8 och 13.
ProValAB2 bidrar till fattigdomsbekämpning, jämställdhet, stärkandet av demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter, klimatanpassning och konfliktförebyggande i Burkina Faso. Denna nya åtgärd kommer att göra det möjligt att adressera olika utmaningar i kontexten, som tillgång till finansiering för jordbruksproducenter, landrättigheter, biologisk mångfald, miljöintegrering, användning av förnybar energi för bevattning, omvandling och bevarande. Insatsen kommer att genomföras mellan december 2021 och december 2024. Det samfinansierade projektet kommer att bekostas av Sverige med cirka 135 000 000 kronor och av Burkina Faso med cirka 6 614 000 kronor. Burkina Fasos jordbruksministerium ansvarar för genomförandet genom en projektledningsenhet, i samarbete med en grupp internationella experter och en översynskommitté.

The project “Value-addition in Agriculture from small dams in Burkina Faso (ProValAB 2)” aims to assure an improved agricultural valorization of hydraulic infrastructure already in place in Burkina Faso. The overall goal of the Small Dam Agricultural Valorization Project is: " Households sustainably develop food security/nutritional security and increase their incomes by exploiting water from small dams through the development of promising value chains ". The ultimate change expected from ProValAB2 is: " The living conditions of households in the project intervention area have improved by exploiting water from small dams through the development of promising value chains ". The project aims to be "gender transformative” and will seek the economic empowerment of women and youth as actors in these same value chains. ProValAB2 will operate in 19 sites distributed in 6 regions: Center, Center-East, Center-North, Center-West, East and Central Plateau. ProValAB2 is part of a dynamic to develop the potential of water bodies and to promote the agricultural economy by creating added value on agricultural production. It emphasizes integrated resource management by promoting equitable access and sustainable use of water resources by the various users (farmers of irrigated crops, breeders, fishermen, fish farmers and their organizations, as well as processors of agricultural and fishery products, water users or households using dams). It is consistent with the priorities of the agricultural sector, which focus on water management, promotion of mechanization, intensification of production and improvement of the processing rate of agricultural products. It contributes to the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially SDGs 1, 2, 8 and 13. ProValAB2 is relevant for poverty alleviation, Gender equality, Democracy and Human Rights, climate change adaptation and conflict prevention in Burkina Faso. This new intervention will make it possible to take into account challenges to be taken up in the context of the development of mechanisms for access to financing for producers, land security, biodiversity, environmental integration, use of renewable energies for irrigation, transformation and conservation. It will be implemented over December 2021-december 2024 co-financed by Sweden and the Government of Burkina Faso with an estimated cost of about 135 000 000 SEK from Sweden and State of Burkina Faso about 6 614 000 SEK. Its implementation will be ensured by the Ministry in charge of Agriculture through a Project Management Unit supported by an International Technical Assistance (ITA) and a Review Committee.
